Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Strathmore School. We are a happy, thriving, oversubscribed and growing special school for children and young people aged 4 -19 years old with complex learning difficulties including those with an additional diagnosis of autism and/or physical/sensory disabilities.
Our aim as a school is to support our learners to self-advocate for themselves, be as independent as possible, be a part of their school and wider community and prepare them for adulthood.
We are one school, however, unique in that we have 4 campuses, all which are co-located with Richmond local mainstream schools.
We work hard to ensure that the quality of the provision is consistent across all campuses so that no child or young person misses out.
At Strathmore School, every learner’s journey in education is personalised and delivered through a flexible curriculum designed around the needs of the learners, their interests and motivators as well as balancing their social and emotional development.
We deliver this through highly skilled staff, supported by Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapists and other professionals to ensure a well-rounded education for all learners. We are committed to working in partnership with parents/carers and believe that consistency, where possible, between home and school provides the best possible outcomes for our learners.
In September 2026 Strathmore became part of Helix Learning Trust, having previously been part of Auriga Academy Trust. We work closely with our partner schools across the Trust and with our co-located mainstream schools to create exciting and meaningful inclusive opportunities for all children and young people.
We hope you find all the information you need on our website. However, if you have any further queries please don’t hesitate to contact the school office. info@strathmore.org.uk

Careers and IAG
Careers guidance and support is an integral part of the curriculum for learners at Strathmore School.
We ensure that learners and families are supported in developing each individual’s career identity, and work hard to ensure that when each learner leaves Strathmore, they are able to actively contribute to their community through a developed level of independence, personalised communication and with the support of their families.
The 14-19 programme is overseen by Adriana Martyr. Learners, parents, teachers and employers can send enquiries via
info@strathmore.org.uk
020 8948 0047 Ext 101
Strathmore School is committed to providing high quality guidance and advice on future pathways. Our Provider Access Policy gives details of how training providers can visit the school to offer eligible learner information and advice about career pathways.
Learners participate in careers learning opportunities that are carefully tailored to each student’s individual needs and are consistent with the eight Gatsby benchmarks:
A stable careers programme
Learning from career and labour market information
Addressing the needs of each pupil
Linking curriculum learning to careers
Encounters with employers and employees
Experiences of workplaces
Encounters with further and higher education
As a school, Strathmore supports careers development through meaningful, personalised work experience opportunities both internally and externally. We expect all learners to develop skills that prepare them for the next steps in their education. The school constantly strives to forge links with the local community to build opportunities for our learners to experience what work looks like, and building relationships with potential placements.
Through our existing partnerships with other colleges, professionals and businesses, we deliver bespoke packages of work experience for students. Students are typically supported by school staff during work experience placements but the nature and level of support offered differs based on the needs of each individual pupil. We welcome feedback from students, families, employers and other stakeholders on an ongoing basis, continually refining and improving our offer to individual pupils based on this feedback.
As well as work experience opportunities, Strathmore supports career development through close links with a number of local Further Education providers. Learners are encouraged to express a preference in terms of their destinations after leaving Strathmore through their EHCP and review processes and once their placement has been confirmed, they are supported to attend their future setting to aid with transition.

PE and Sports Premium
The funding has been provided to promote and encourage children to participate in a range of physical activity, both in and out of school, to prevent our pupils from becoming part of the concerning statistics relating to rising obesity rates. PE and Sports Premium funding has jointly been provided by the Department for Education, the Department for Health and Culture and the Department for Media and Sport. It has been allocated to primary school Headteachers and is ring-fenced to be spent on the provision of PE and sport in schools. The Government believes that Headteachers and school leaders should decide how to use the funding for PE and Sports in school. Since the introduction of the PE and Sports Premium, Strathmore School has used the funding to improve the quality of PE and the amount of inclusive sporting opportunities offered to the students.
In 2017-2018, Strathmore’s Primary funding allocation was £16,250. During this time, Strathmore School relocated onto new purpose built facilities over three sites and the lead PE teacher changed. Due to these significant changes in provision, the money was held in order to spend time training the lead PE teacher and researching appropriate resources suitable for the changing cohort of students.
Please refer to the policies section to read the PE and Sports Premiunm Statement.

Current Vacancies
Strathmore is a forward-thinking and innovative Special School based in purpose built accommodation co-located with local, inclusive minded mainstream schools.
We are a happy, thriving, oversubscribed and growing special school for children and young people aged 4 -19 with severe and complex learning difficulties including those with an additional diagnosis of autism and/or physical/sensory disabilities. We are committed to supporting all of our learners to achieve and enjoy and be stimulated and challenged to fulfil their potential. Our highly qualified and dedicated staff have high expectations of our learners and we all have the highest expectations of ourselves.
Our learners are at the heart of our vision and we believe that together we make a positive difference. Our school provides real opportunities for aspiring teachers, school leaders and support staff who want to work in a special educational needs environment.
We recognise that the success of our school is largely dependent on the quality of our staff and are committed to recruiting and retaining outstanding individuals.
If you have any questions about our current vacancies or recruitment process, please contact the Helix Learning Trust HR Team - Richmond Schools.
0203146 1441 hrrichmond@helixlearningtrust.org.uk
Volunteers
All of our schools and the Trust welcome applications from anyone who wishes to volunteer.
To ensure the trust adheres to Keeping Children Safe in Education 2022, all those aged 16 and above volunteering in regulated activity will be subject to an enhanced (with barring) DBS check. No volunteering will be available for those under 16 years old, unless at one of the co-linked schools.
We will be offering two types of placements this academic year, either a weekly placement or a block work placement. The weekly placement will be a minimum commitment of 1 hour per week. This will be tailored to your availability and ideal for a college/ 6th form/ university student. The other placement will be a block of either one or two weeks - this is best suited for work experience. All will be offered on a first come, first served basis. In certain circumstances, we may offer an extension for a volunteer to stay longer with us. This will only be offered once discussed and confirmed by senior leaders and HR.
Students requiring work placements as part of their degree or placement will be offered them by the heads of school if there is suitable availability and their university has completed the necessary safeguarding checks.
Weekly placements: 2026/27 dates coming soon
Work experience placement – 1/2 weeks available to those wishing to undertake a work placement. Please apply at least three weeks prior to the intended placement to allow plenty of time.
Applications will be paused during the very busy recruitment times in the window period.

Ofsted
In Feb 24, Ofsted stated that Strathmore has
‘an ambitious and bespoke curriculum that support pupils to achieve well. The content and order of the curriculum help pupils to develop their communication, literacy and mathematic skills very well.’
This shows the positive impact of the previous 3 years of work to create, implement and embed our Strathmore Developmental Skills Framework (SDSK).
We are aspirational for all our learners, and this is reflected in the personalised EHCP outcomes. Ofsted said in Feb 24, ‘The curriculum is personalised so that everyone can work towards achieving their targets on their education health and care (EHC) plans. For example, in the early years some children learn about capacity using sand, water and containers. This learning is built on with older pupils following recipes to make cakes for the café and stocktaking in the tuck shop.’
In Feb 24, Ofsted evidenced that ‘Communication, language and reading are priorities for all pupils. From the start of early years through to the sixth form there is a well-thought-out programme. Every opportunity is used for pupils to develop their communication skills. For example, during lunchtime, staff encourage pupils to communicate their thoughts and to make choices. This includes through the skilful use of resources. Pupils show their love of books by following stories and looking through books independently. Pupils’ early reading is developed effectively through a consistently delivered phonics programme. Pupils have books that match the sounds they are learning. Their books and recall activities in lessons support pupils to develop some fluency in early reading.’

School Fund
Schools everywhere are facing significant funding pressures. Rising costs and static or decreasing budgets mean that it is increasingly difficult to provide the enriching opportunities and additional resources that help pupils thrive.
These are often the areas hit hardest, yet they are the very things that make school an inspiring and enjoyable place for our children.
To help protect these opportunities, we have a Strathmore School Fund made up of voluntary contributions from parents and carers. This fund supports workshops, special events, software, classroom resources, and equipment — the “extras” that go beyond the basics and make a real difference to our pupils’ experience.
The School Fund gives you the opportunity to make either a one-off donation or a regular contribution that suits your budget. We are very aware of the many financial pressures on families, so we are genuinely grateful for anything you feel able to contribute. Your support really does make a difference to what we can offer our students.
Thank you very much for your generosity and for being part of the Strathmore community.
For further information on how to donate and FAQ's, please see below.
How do I contribute?
Contributions to Strathmore School Fund can be made using the following methods:
Standing Order: Please set up a monthly standing order to this bank account:
The Helix Learning Trust
Account number 84560360
Please quote reference: CLA donate + your surname

You will be given the option to gift aid. In the message section, please state your name so we know who has made the donation. Leave it blank if you wish to remain anonymous.

The Helix Learning Trust

FAQ's
Can I Gift Aid my payment?
Academy trusts, as exempt charities, are eligible to claim Gift Aid on voluntary donations made by UK taxpayers. Gift Aid allows the Trust to reclaim the basic rate of income tax on donations for all schools within the Trust, effectively increasing the value of eligible donations by 25% at no extra cost to the donor. For every £1 you donate, we can get an extra 25p from HMRC at no extra cost to you. Find out more about on the GOV.UK website: https://www.gov.uk/donating-to-charity/gift-aid.
If you are a UK taxpayer please email the school office to receive a Gift Aid form.
How much should I contribute?
This is up to you and depends on your personal circumstances. For regular monthly contributions we suggest between £10 and £20 per month, but we ask those parents and carers who can afford it to give more please. If you are a UK taxpayer we politely request a minimum monthly donation of £10 or a minimum one-off donation of £50 to keep the administration of the Gift Aid scheme justifiable. However, we are very grateful for any amount you can give via the non-Gift Aid account.
Will my child be affected if I cannot pay?
The donation is voluntary and confidential; not making a payment will not affect your child in any way.
